value.baseline: FP16 FasterTransformer (OPT-13B and OPT-30B context stage)

ev.quote: compared to FasterTransformer's FP16 implementation of OPT, SmoothQuant-O3 can further reduce the execution latency of OPT-13B and OPT-30B by up to 1.56× when using a single GPU.

strengths.value: Maintains FP16 accuracy on OPT-175B, BLOOM-176B and GLM-130B with INT8 W8A8, while baselines like W8A8 naive and ZeroQuant collapse.

ev.quote: SmoothQuant can match the FP16 accuracy on all evaluation datasets with all quantization schemes.

strengths.value: Hardware-friendly: uses standard INT8 GEMM kernels via per-tensor static activation quantization, avoiding LLM.int8() mixed-precision overhead.

ev.quote: Our algorithm preserves the performance of LLMs (up to 176B, the largest open-source LLM we can find) with an efficient per-tensor, static quantization scheme without retraining

strengths.value: Delivers up to 1.56× speedup and ~2× memory saving and serves MT-NLG 530B on a single 8×A100 node.

ev.quote: We integrate SmoothQuant into PyTorch and FasterTransformer, getting up to 1.56× inference acceleration and halving the memory footprint.

strengths.value: Training-free with only 512 calibration sentences; one calibration generalises to all downstream zero-shot tasks.

ev.quote: we calibrate the smoothing factors and the static quantization step sizes once with 512 random sentences from the pre-training dataset Pile, and apply the same smoothed and quantized model for all downstream tasks.

weaknesses.value: Migration strength α must be hand-tuned per model family (0.5 for OPT/BLOOM, 0.75 for GLM-130B, 0.6–0.9 for Llama/Falcon/Mistral).

ev.quote: we can choose a larger α to migrate more quantization difficulty to weights (like 0.75).

weaknesses.value: GLM-130B needs additional 2% top-token clipping during static calibration to recover accuracy.

ev.quote: Note that we clip the top 2% tokens when calibrating the static quantization step sizes for GLM-130B following Wei et al. (2022).

weaknesses.value: Per-tensor static O3 setting still loses ~0.8–1% accuracy on BLOOM-176B and GLM-130B versus FP16.

ev.quote: the O3 level (per-tensor static) degrades the average accuracy by 0.8%, which we attribute to the discrepancy between the statically collected statistics and the real evaluation samples'

weaknesses.value: Direct comparison with weight-only methods like GPTQ is avoided due to incompatible kernels and serving frameworks.

ev.quote: we were trying to compare our method with GPTQ (Frantar et al., 2022) but found it difficult due to different implementations.

limitations.value: Only INT8 W8A8 is studied; lower-bit (INT4) weight or activation quantization is left as future work.

ev.quote: we can integrate GPTQ's method for a better weight quantization and potentially achieve W4A4 quantization, which will lead to even better hardware efficiency... We leave this exploration to future work.

limitations.value: All experiments run on data-center A100 GPUs; no edge or mobile hardware is tested.

ev.quote: All our experiments are conducted on NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU servers.

limitations.value: Safety, bias, jailbreak and refusal behaviour after quantization are not evaluated.
KV-cache quantization is mentioned as motivation but is not implemented or measured in this work.

ev.quote: the memory size of the KV cache can no longer be ignored... In this case, quantization of activation can also help reduce the memory cost from storing the KV cache.

future_work_stated.value: Integrate GPTQ-style weight quantization with SmoothQuant to reach W4A4 on Hopper INT4 instructions.

ev.quote: we can integrate GPTQ's method for a better weight quantization and potentially achieve W4A4 quantization, which will lead to even better hardware efficiency (INT4 instructions are supported on NVIDIA's Hopper GPU architecture).

future_work_stated.value: Inspire future research into why different model/training designs have different quantization difficulties.

ev.quote: Note that different model/training designs have different quantization difficulties, which we hope will inspire future research.
